newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian state sugar firm sold to Ivorian group.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian state sugar firm sold to Ivorian group.

text.p: Ivory Coast has sold a majority stake in part of state sugar firm Societe pour le Developpement des Plantations de Canne a Sucre (SODESUCRE) to a consortium led by Ivorian commodities group SIFCA, a government cabinet meeting statement said on Wednesday.

The consortium would take a 55 percent shareholding in lot B of SODESUCRE -- which is being privatised as two separate blocks -- by paying 16.8 billion CFA francs and agreeing to take on two billion CFA of attached debts, the statement added.
SIFCA's consortium partners are Mauritian sugar firm Harel freres and another firm, Rial Trading, the statement said.
Ivory Coast had said it would retain a 20 percent stake in SODESUCRE. Another 20 percent stake be floated on Abidjan's bourse and employees would take the remaining five percent.
Both lots A and B comprise two production plants and surounding plantations.
Senegal's Cie Sucriere Senegalaise had put in a similar bid for lot B, which is made up of plants in northwest and central Ivory Coast.

Bidders for lot A included a group comprising British commodities trader ED & F Man Group PLC and Britain's Commonwealth Development Corporation, an overseas finance institution. A winner for lot A has not been declared.
